preamble: Four down solutions are partially clued and connected with a comma.

clue.text: Curls connected less closely with the above

definitions.meaning: long spiralling locks of hair hanging down

definitions.text: connected less closely with the above
definitions.meaning: the Ringlet is a brown butterfly, a more distant relative of the Comma named in the preamble than the themed down answers

explanation.surface: A hairdressing note about curls that hang more loosely than those described earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: The preamble's 'comma' is the Comma butterfly; the four partly clued down answers are its close relatives, while the Ringlet belongs to a different branch of the same family.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanging spiral locks of hair are called by this name, a standard synonym for curls.

clue.text: Male, summoned, went wild

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
paged means called over a public address

explanation.surface: A man who was called and then ran amok.
explanation.definitionFit: To rampage is to rush about violently, so went wild is a past-tense synonym.

clue.text: See 19
Song about small rise in latitude

indicators.note: the song goes around the other piece

parts.note: a lay is a ballad or song

indicators.note: in a down clue the word goes upwards, so it is read backwards

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small

explanation.surface: A ballad about a slight increase in latitude on a voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise' works only because this is a down clue: the small word is read upwards. WEE is Scottish for small.
explanation.definitionFit: Room for manoeuvre or freedom of action is a synonym for latitude.

clue.text: The wrong love is two points to damnation

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
O is love, a zero score in tennis
taken as written
E is east, a compass point
S is south, another compass point
hell is the place of the damned

explanation.surface: A sermon warning that loving wrongly takes you two steps closer to damnation.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue has no definition: the preamble says these down answers are butterflies related to the Comma. TORT, O, IS, E, S and HELL make the Tortoiseshell.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tortoiseshell is a mottled orange butterfly in the same group as the Comma butterfly named in the preamble.

clue.text: Attack on the community?

definitions.meaning: to rush at an enemy, as a cavalry does
a levy placed on the community

explanation.surface: A question about some assault on the neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: The Community Charge was the local tax (the 'poll tax') brought in by Margaret Thatcher's government; a charge on the community is a tax levied on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A headlong rush at the enemy is a military synonym for an attack.

clue.text: Apocalyptic 4 seem out of order in the Cape

indicators.note: the rearranged word sits inside the cape

parts.note: Cape Horn, the southern tip of South America

indicators.note: the word seem is out of order, so it is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Four doom-laden riders appear in disorder at the Cape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of order' turns SEEM into SEME, which goes 'in' HORN. The Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse appear in the Book of Revelation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Book of Revelation names four riders, Conquest, War, Famine and Death, who bring the end of the world.

clue.text: It's true about parent station in space

indicators.note: the word for genuine goes round the others

parts.note: real means true or genuine
dad is a father
Mir was the Soviet and Russian space station

explanation.surface: Confirms a story about a parent working on an orbiting station.
explanation.walkthrough: No definition: the preamble makes this a butterfly linked with the Comma. REAL goes 'about' DAD and MIR. 'It's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Red Admiral is a black butterfly with red bands, a close relative of the Comma named in the preamble.

clue.text: Don't initiate endearment (funny one) for hearing aid

indicators.note: the term of affection must not start, so it loses its first letter

parts.note: heart, as in 'dear heart', a term of affection
rum means odd or funny
pet, another endearment, the funny one of the parenthesis

explanation.surface: Advice to skip a soppy pet name, with an odd aside, in favour of a hearing aid.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket is wordplay, not an aside: 'one' is a second endearment, and it is a funny one, RUM PET. 'Don't initiate' strips H from HEART.
explanation.definitionFit: This horn-shaped device held to the ear was the old-fashioned hearing aid.

clue.text: The never ending cheese?

definitions.meaning: Agatha Christie's play The ... has run in London's West End since 1952
a device baited with a lump of cheese, and by extension cheap poor-quality cheese

explanation.surface: A question about some cheese that never runs out.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mousetrap is the world's longest-running stage play; 'mousetrap cheese' is a slang term for inferior cheese, the sort used as bait.
explanation.definitionFit: Agatha Christie's play is famous for a run that never seems to end, and cheese is the classic bait for the trap.

clue.text: Appropriate colour for ruler

parts.note: purple is the imperial colour, born in the purple
an emperor is a supreme ruler

explanation.surface: Purple as the fitting colour for a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: No definition: the preamble makes this a butterfly linked with the Comma. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Purple Emperor is a large woodland butterfly in the same family as the Comma named in the preamble.

clue.text: One of 6 in addition from 12

annotationWithheld.why: Clue 'One of 6 in addition from 12' (RIDER): 'One of 6' (a horseman) and 'in addition' (a rider clause) are clear, but no reading of 'from 12' (LABOUR LEADER) gives RIDER, and no blog for this puzzle was found.

clue.text: He (or she) could be red (or blue) à la mode

indicators.note: says the following letters could be rearranged into the answer
à la mode means fashioned in a new style, so the letters are refashioned

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written, ignoring the accent

explanation.surface: A party chief of either sex might wear the colours red or blue, depending on fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' and 'mode' together signal the anagram of RED OR BLUE A LA. Red is Labour's colour, blue the Conservatives'; New Labour was said to have turned blue.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of Britain's Labour Party may be a man or a woman, so the clue's pronoun stands for that person.

clue.text: Candidate for Miss SE5?

parts.note: SE5 is the London postcode of Camberwell
a beauty is a contestant in a Miss pageant

explanation.surface: A question about a contestant for a local beauty title in south London.
explanation.walkthrough: No definition: the preamble makes this a butterfly linked with the Comma. Camberwell is a district of south London.
explanation.definitionFit: The Camberwell Beauty is a rare dark butterfly with cream edges, a close relative of the Comma in the preamble.

clue.text: Politic mad? Politic mad

indicators.note: the second mad says the words before it go crazy and rearrange

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bemused exchange about whether politics is mad, answered with a flat yes.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as question and answer. The first 'Politic' is the definition; 'mad? Politic' is the fodder and the second 'mad' says to rearrange it.
explanation.definitionFit: Politic means shrewd and tactful, and a tactful person is a diplomat, so the two adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: The "A" Team's maybe one of evil

definitions.note: a reference to the 'axis of evil', George W. Bush's phrase

parts.note: a team in cricket or football is an eleven, XI, and the 's is joined on

explanation.surface: Asks whether the 1980s TV action squad might count among the evildoers.
explanation.walkthrough: XI (eleven, a side) with the 's gives XIS. George W. Bush called Iran, Iraq and North Korea the 'axis of evil'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'axis of evil' supplies the word missing from the definition, a group of hostile states.

clue.text: "Stomach" is "tum": "lips" are wrong

indicators.note: the letters of the words before it are wrong, so they must be put right by rearranging

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mock-pedantic ruling that saying tum for stomach is fine but lips is the wrong word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link; 'wrong' rearranges TUM LIPS ARE. 'Stomach' here is a ruminant's third stomach, which a cow, sheep or deer has.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the anatomical name for the third compartment of a ruminant's stomach, also called the omasum.

clue.text: Pit not reserved for people on stage

definitions.note: an adjective, as in an opencast pit or mine

parts.note: open means available to all, not booked
the cast are the actors in a play

explanation.surface: Theatre seating: a pit that has not been reserved for the actors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pit' and 'stage' set a theatre scene, but the pit is a mine. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A mine dug from the surface rather than underground is called this, the kind of pit worked open to the sky.

clue.text: The Queen before William, then, one that needs hoarding

parts.note: Bill is the short form of William
The Queen before William means William comes after the Queen, and post means after
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A line of royal succession: Elizabeth, then a king William, and then someone who needs a hoard.
explanation.walkthrough: The royal order is the trick: if Elizabeth comes before William, William comes after (post) her. 'then' is a link, and a hoarding is a large advertising board, not a stockpile.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who pastes up advertisements needs a large board, a hoarding, to stick them on.

clue.text: Starving in the party sense?

parts.note: a rave is a big dance party
nous is common sense or know-how

explanation.surface: Asks whether going hungry is meant in the party sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Being extremely hungry is a synonym for starving, used loosely in everyday speech.

clue.text: See 13
Miss Marple's mentor endlessly seen at classical shrines

indicators.note: to miss is to go astray, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of Marple's, with its S kept

indicators.note: the word mentor loses its last letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Agatha Christie's sleuth's mentor turns up at ancient shrines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' looks like Miss Marple's title but is the anagram signal; 'endlessly' cuts MENTOR to MENTO. MARPLES plus MENTO is rearranged. 'seen at' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Places of worship built in ancient Rome are classical shrines by definition, being in the Graeco-Roman style.

clue.text: Cairo, Istanbul, Tripoli and York, for starters

definitions.text: Cairo, Istanbul, Tripoli and York, for starters

indicators.note: starters come at the beginning of a meal, so the opening letter of each place is used

explanation.surface: A list of cities to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: The initials of the four places spell the answer, and every one of them is an example of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cairo, Istanbul, Tripoli and York are all large towns, so each is an example of the answer.

clue.text: See 1
More outside?

definitions.meaning: the Latin prefix ...- means outside, as in extramural

explanation.surface: Asks whether more is waiting outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something additional is more of it, and the Latin word behind the prefix means beyond or outside.

clue.text: Psychiatrist grasping return of satisfaction voiced during corporal punishment

indicators.note: one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: R. D. Laing was a famous Scottish psychiatrist

indicators.note: the word for contentment voiced by a cat is read backwards

parts.note: a purr is the sound a contented cat makes

explanation.surface: A psychiatrist hearing contentment expressed during a caning session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return of' turns PURR into RRUP, which LAING holds ('grasping'). 'during' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This dialect word means a thrashing or beating, so it is a form of corporal punishment.

clue.text: Commander has died outside site

indicators.note: one word wraps round the other

parts.note: late means dead, having died
OC is Officer Commanding

explanation.surface: A commanding officer has died somewhere outside the base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a link. 'site' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To site something is to place it in position, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Good lots of solvers in red, with iris not in spectrum

indicators.note: the repeated pronoun goes inside the colour

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the pronoun is repeated, more than once

parts.note: ye is an old plural for you, the solvers being addressed

explanation.surface: A good crowd of crossword fans dressed in red, one with eyes of an unusual colour.
explanation.walkthrough: YE is the old plural 'you', addressing the solvers. Grey is not one of the colours of the rainbow, and the iris is the coloured part of the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Having irises of a colour absent from the rainbow describes eyes coloured grey.
